catalogue.name: Catalogue
catalogue.definition: A long list of objects or names used in place of narrative.

disguise.name: Disguise
disguise.definition: A character adopting another identity in full view of the audience.

double-plot.name: The double plot
double-plot.definition: Two parallel stories staged so that each comments on the other.

epigram.name: Epigram
epigram.definition: A generalisation compressed into a single balanced sentence.

frame-narrative.name: Frame narrative
frame-narrative.definition: A story enclosed within another story, often several layers deep.

gothic.name: Gothic machinery
gothic.definition: Bells, darkness, apparitions, graves and locked rooms used to produce dread.

idiolect.name: Idiolect
idiolect.definition: Giving each character a distinct and consistent way of speaking.

landscape.name: Landscape as pressure
landscape.definition: Using terrain, weather and scale to exert force on the characters rather than to decorate them.

retrospective-narration.name: Retrospective narration
retrospective-narration.definition: An account given after the event by a narrator who already knows how it ends.

song.name: Song
song.definition: Sung lyric used to carry information a speech cannot.

symbolic-objects.name: Objects and omens
symbolic-objects.definition: Things in the narrative that carry a meaning the characters half-register.

thresholds.name: Doors and thresholds
thresholds.definition: Physical barriers used to carry an idea about what is concealed behind them.
